transcription:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Cerulean CTO), Ethan Brooks (Cerulean ML Eng), Ana Ruiz (Cerulean Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 40 minutes. quick intros real quick?
[00:07] Maya: Hi I'm Maya CTO at Cerulean Health, we run patient-facing NLP and triage workflows. Ethan's our ML lead.
[00:12] Ethan: hey all, small infra team.
[00:14] Ana: Ana from security, i'll be poking at compliance stuff.
[00:17] Jordan: Great. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. Today we'll do a PLG quickstart walkthrough: free credits, time-to-first-token, and also map your path from hosted -> dedicated -> private.
[00:30] Priya: Quick note, we often get customers spinning up in under an hour with our quickstart - you can get to first token with API keys, quick SDK, and a small sample. We also provide starter prompts and examples for triage use cases.
[00:45] Maya: That's great. Our priority is evaluating hosted first for speed to prototype. If it works we may want dedicated GPUs for predictable throughput. Eventually private for PHI/data residency if the pilot scales.
[01:02] Jordan: Totally expected. Curious about your constraints - latency target, budget, timeline?
[01:10] Ethan: Latency target for the user flows is 300-500ms p95 for short prompts (<=128 tokens). Cost is important - we run a lot of small requests. Timeline: we'd like to prove value in 2-3 weeks.
[01:27] Ana: From security side, we need SOC2 compliance, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and key management (KMS/HSM integration). Also data retention policies and ability to delete data on demand.
[01:40] Priya: Makes sense. For SOC2 and security we have docs we can share, and Redwood's Private deployment supports full VPC/on-prem options and KMS integration. For hosted we do offer SOC2 and audit logs, and we have contractual clauses for data handling - i'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:05] Maya: Good. Can you explain the difference between hosted, dedicated, and private in practical terms?
[02:12] Jordan: Sure. Hosted API is self-serve: you get API keys + free credits, quick onboarding. Good for fast prototyping and early PLG adoption. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity - predictable latency and throughput, better for production traffic. Private is customer-managed network control plane for compliance (VPC/on-prem). We can route requests to the appropriate tier as you grow.
[02:38] Ethan: For benchmarking, what do you suggest we measure?
[02:42] Priya: Basic latency p50/p95, throughput for batch workloads, token costs (per-inference token), and quality regression vs your baseline model. We can run a quick bench on our hosted env and give you numbers; but for final production you may want to run on dedicated to see real latencies.
[03:00] Jordan: Also important: batching, prefix KV cache and quantization can drastically change cost/latency tradeoffs. Our Optimize recommendations can suggest quantization profile for your workload.
[03:12] Ethan: You mentioned KV cash earlier?
[03:14] Priya: sorry i said K V cache - the KV cache is our prefix/key-value cache for repeated context, it reduces recompute for streaming chats.
[03:22] Maya: About free credits - what's included and expiry?
[03:26] Jordan: PLG free credits typically enough for initial prototyping (we'll include details in the quickstart email). They expire in 90 days usually. Time-to-first-token is often under 15 minutes if you follow the quickstart: sign up, get API key, run the simple curl or SDK snippet.
[03:43] Ana: For hosted, how do you handle data residency and deletion requests?
[03:47] Priya: Hosted has data controls and retention settings; we also support delete-on-demand via API and contractual commitments. For strict residency we recommend Private deployments where data stays inside your VPC or on-prem.
[03:59] Ethan: Are there cases where hosted won't meet latency?
[04:02] Priya: For strict p95 <200ms at scale, you often need dedicated GPUs co-located with your traffic region; hosted is multi-tenant but we have regional endpoints and fallbacks.
[04:12] Maya: Any gotchas on compatibility if we start on hosted and move to dedicated/private?
[04:17] Jordan: We've designed the API and model catalog to be consistent; you can pin model versions and rollouts independent of infra. Some variant models or quantization may differ, so you'll want to run your evals during the migration.
[04:30] Ethan: On the model side, do you host open models or proprietary ones?
[04:33] Priya: We host a curated catalog of open models and Redwood-verified profiles; we also support custom model variants on Dedicated/Private if you bring your model.
[04:44] Maya: Security team would like the SOC2 report and SAML integration docs.
[04:47] Ana: yes, and the KMS/HSM integration detail. Also we'd like to know if you have penetration testing or third-party reports.
[04:56] Jordan: We'll send the security pack and SOC2 attestation. We do pentest regularly - i'll include the summary plus the contact for our compliance team.
[05:05] Priya: For the benchmark i'll need a small sample dataset and some representative prompts - then i can run a hosted quick bench and return p50/p95 numbers and per-token cost.
[05:15] Ethan: we can provide a 200-record sample of anonymized triage prompts.
[05:19] Maya: Timeline - we want a pilot in two weeks, so if we get the bench results next week that would work.
[05:24] Jordan: Sounds good. We'll aim to get the bench by 03/10.
[05:28] [longer section of technical Q&A]
[05:30] Ethan: How do you handle streaming and tool calling? We have a step that calls external APIs from the model.
[05:35] Priya: We support streaming responses and function/tool calling patterns; there are structured-output helpers in the SDKs. For private deployments we'd instrument tracing hooks for observability.
[05:45] Ethan: On observability - can we get token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards?
[05:49] Priya: Yes Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdown, per-model dashboards and tracing. We can also set up alerts for quality regressions.
[06:00] Maya: Pricing - is hosted per-token and dedicated via committed capacity?
[06:03] Jordan: Exactly, hosted is usage-based (per-token). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commit and predictable throughput. We can share pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[06:12] Ana: Contractual SLA options for dedicated?
[06:15] Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; for enterprise private we can do custom SLAs.
[06:20] Ethan: For benchmarking, would priya run a test of 1000 short prompts and stream results?
[06:25] Priya: yes i can run p50/p95 and throughput with concurrency, and also measure cost per 1k tokens.
[06:33] Maya: Are there known integrations with SSO providers?
[06:36] Jordan: Yes we support SAML/SSO with the usual providers (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace).
[06:41] [small crosstalk about scheduling]
[06:50] Jordan: recap of next steps: i'll send pricing + quickstart + security pack; priya will run benchmark with the sample data; maya to share sample and SSO info; schedule pilot kickoff next week depending on results.
[07:05] Maya: ok thanks everyone.
[07:07] Jordan: Thanks - we'll follow up no later than next Friday.

End of transcript.
Notes/Artifacts referenced: quickstart guide (link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart), security pack (link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack), benchmark template spreadsheet (link: internal)
